note: Ground truth used only to score the detector offline; never a controller input.
corrective_iterations: iter0: synthetic-tuned bar mask -> detection_rate 0.10, pose 0.0 on real gates (FAIL: rejected the saturated green gate)
iter1: reuse the frozen v1 detector pixel classifier -> detection_rate 0.25, pose 0.10; distance ~0.65m OK but yaw unreliable (median 139deg, sign 0.0)
verdict: DETECTOR NOT YET RELIABLE ON REAL IMAGES: aperture-corner detection is the bottleneck (thin green bars + haze + ~3.9m distance rarely yield a clean quadrilateral). Distance/lateral are usable when a quad is found; gate-plane YAW from geometric PnP is not trustworthy. A learned corner/pose detector (or further CV iteration) is required before observation-v2 can improve the controller.
recommendation: Keep the frozen center-only v1 controller as the best available. Do not wire pose features into a v2 policy until yaw-sign accuracy on real images is reliable.
